pr_title: executor: Fix tidb crash on index merge reader
pr_body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:

2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #40877

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?
Let both `pickAndExecTask` and `handlePickAndExecTaskPanic` take the address of `task` as its argument, so once `*task` is assigned in `pickAndExecTask`,  `handlePickAndExecTaskPanic` will get a non nil value.

issue_context.title: TiDB may crash if Index Merge reader meet error
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
1. in https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/ee758bcf8b68ad52ce46cfe9d42647f71614ee26/executor/index_merge_reader.go#L611-L620
the init value of `task` is nil, and it will be assigned by `task = worker.pickAndExecTask(ctx1)`, and it is also be passed as an argument of `worker.handlePickAndExecTaskPanic(ctx1, task)`
2. in https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/ee758bcf8b68ad52ce46cfe9d42647f71614ee26/executor/index_merge_reader.go#L1133-L1143
the recover function will call `task.doneCh <- err4Panic` directly without check if the `task` is nill or not, if `task` is nil, tidb will hit SIGSEGV. A typical crash stack is

review_comments:
It looks like the main point of this PR is to assign to the `task` here, so that even if we panic in `executeTask`, `startIndexMergeTableScanWorker` and `handlePickAndExecTaskPanic` could also get the `doneCh`.

I think it's not easy to realize this. I suggest we add some comments to clarify it.
OK, I've add some comments to explain why need use the address of `task` here.
